title: A fair transition to another shared form
meaning: Your union can change a familiar routine with care when fair actions and adjustment leave room for the emotional ending of an earlier form.
text: In your partnership, transition can develop through clear actions and attentive adjustment. In the physical position, Justice expresses fair choices and responsibility for consequences. In energy, Temperance encourages combining different needs without erasing them. In emotions, Death conveys the ending of a familiar form. Another arrangement may already suit you both while the earlier one still brings sadness. Practical agreement need not immediately finish a personal response. Two people can recognise a useful choice while needing different amounts of time to release the expectations and familiar details attached to what came before.

For example, you replace monthly trips with a large group with calmer meetings. You fairly complete promises and discuss what to preserve in another format. The new measure is comfortable, yet the familiar scale is still missed. **A considerate transition can hold both a suitable choice and sadness for the earlier form.** Different speeds of adjustment need not make the change mistaken or turn longing into proof of insufficient commitment to today’s decision.

It becomes harder if adjustment must make completion painless. You avoid upsetting anyone, delay a clear boundary and maintain the earlier form beyond available capacity. Harmony becomes preservation of something exhausted. Freedom grows when a limit can be named and feelings given time. You can respect the past without endlessly sustaining its timetable, gradually finding continuation without identical delight in every new condition.
